title: kv-cache: memory manager + adaptive eviction heuristics v39 (spillover, paging, defrag coalescing)
author: Evelyn Park
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and suboptimal spillover/paging behavior continue to cause tail-latency spikes under high-concurrency, mixed-sequence workloads. This PR implements a new memory manager and adaptive eviction heuristics (v39) that combine lightweight on-GPU compaction coalescing, tiered paging thresholds, and spillover prioritization to preserve hot KV segments while reducing unnecessary I/O and defragmentation overhead. Key changes: 1) new MemoryManager component with slab-aware allocation and live-fragmentation tracking; 2) adaptive eviction policy that blends LRU-decay with segment hotness score computed from access-frequency, sequence-length-weighted token cost, and request-priority tags; 3) spillover scheduler that coordinates with the continuous-batcher to avoid evicting segments that are likely to be reused within batching windows; 4) on-device compaction kernel that coalesces adjacent freed ranges (best-effort, bounded work per tick) to reduce fragmentation without blocking inference; 5) tuning knobs exposed via runtime config (target_free_ratio, paging_high/warn/low thresholds, compaction_budget_ms) and metrics. Performance: in internal perf-canary runs (mixed chat + long-context sampling) this reduced 99.9th latency by ~23% and lowered GPU offload IOPS by ~34% for high-fragmentation scenarios. Rollout: feature-flagged, gradual rollout to Dedicated pools with canary group for 48h, metrics and regression alerts wired to Console. See linked Linear tickets ENG-3456 and ENG-4120 for evaluation artifacts and canary dashboards. Checklist: - [x] MemoryManager implementation and unit tests - [x] Eviction heuristics and end-to-end integration tests - [x] Kernel compaction prototype and microbenchmarks - [x] CI perf job and canary dashboard updates - [x] Docs: runtime config and admin tuning notes
